title: surea11y-lab app configuration
description: What the app's Save configuration writes and Load configuration reads: the form as the user left it ("state"), the run spec it comes to ("runSpec"), and the batch rows when there are any. `node src/cli/run-workflow.js <config.json>` runs one too. Generated from src/workflow/action-definitions.js by `npm run build:action-docs`; do not edit schemas/app-config.v1.schema.json by hand.

id.description: What runCustomStep's customStepId names. Unique in the spec.

action.a11yScan.title: A11y scan
action.a11yScan.description: Run an accessibility scan on the current page or within a selector. You can narrow the scan to a region using 'context' and exclude noisy areas using 'exclude'.

disabled.description: Skip this step without removing it.

collapsed.description: Shown folded in the app's builder. No effect on the run.

alias.description: The step's own title in the app's builder and in the run's log, in place of its type's.

label.description: Label shown in reports and live stream. Supports {var:name}, {index}, {oneBased}, {total}.

scanTags.description: Free-form tags for this scan. Used to filter the report by tag once the run finishes. Supports {var:name}, {index}, {oneBased}, {total}, so a single tag like {var:viewport} fills in per iteration. Pick tags already used elsewhere in this workflow or add new ones.

context.description: The parts of the page this scan checks: every element these CSS selectors match, comma separated. Empty, the scan checks the whole page. A selector that matches nothing scans nothing, and the report says so.

exclude.description: The parts of the page this scan leaves out: every element these CSS selectors match, comma separated.

includeBestPractice.description: Also run the best-practice rules in this scan: good practice beyond the profile, such as landmarks and heading order. The profile alone never runs them. Their findings are listed in a Best practices section of their own and count toward no criterion, score, compliance rate or comparison.

profile.description: What this scan checks against, WCAG 2.2 AA unless it says otherwise: WCAG 2.2 at Level A, AA or AAA, or a standard, which sets the WCAG version and the level, all of them Level A and AA: EN 301 549 V4.1.1, the EU standard, which is WCAG 2.2, and EN 301 549 V3.2.1, its earlier version, which is WCAG 2.1 and still checks 4.1.1 Parsing. surea11y applies a standard in full, version details such as 4.1.1 included. A list checks against several at once, such as ["wcag22-aa", "wai-aria-1.2"]: one WCAG level at most, since each includes the ones below it, and any standards. Each one judges the page as a scan of it alone would, and a finding that fails any of them fails the scan; a finding says what each one makes of it. A variable may hold one profile or several separated by commas. Including rule IDs or tags explicitly takes precedence over a standard. Passing the rules does not mean the page meets the standard: many criteria still need a manual check.

anyOf.description: a profile of an installed standard pack

locale.description: Language surea11y writes its findings in: rule titles, what failed, how to fix it, and the WCAG criteria names. Rules that judge wording, such as vague link text or generic headings, go by the language of the page, not this setting.

anyOf.description: text with a {var:…} token

applyDefaultStyle.description: Blur and fade the parts of the page the scan leaves out (Exclude selectors, and what is outside Context) in the scan's screenshots, so they show what was checked.

preserveHover.description: Keep current :hover styling for this scan/evidence capture. Disable to clear transient hover before capture.

waitTimeout.description: How long Wait for waits for its selector before the step fails.

anyOf.description: a number as text, or text with a {var:…} token

stageTimeout.description: The most each stage of the scan may take before it is given up on: loading the engine into the page, letting the page settle, the page ready wait, the check itself and the screenshot. Pictures of flagged elements get their own time on top.

anyOf.description: a number as text, or text with a {var:…} token

pageReadyTimeout.description: Before scanning, wait up to this long for the page to finish loading: the load event, web fonts and images (not lazy ones). If it has not finished by then, the scan runs anyway and its report says what was still loading. 0 checks without waiting.

anyOf.description: a number as text, or text with a {var:…} token

frames.description: Scan the content of the page's iframes as well, each whole, and report what they show with the page: an element in an iframe names the iframe it is in. An iframe the page doesn't show, that the scan excludes or leaves outside its Include, or that shows nothing is left out, and the report says which and why; one under aria-hidden is scanned for what is seen, not for names and roles. Off, the default, the page's own content is scanned and the report says how many iframes were left out.

heavyNodeThreshold.description: A page with more elements than this (its shadow roots' included) is still scanned in full, and its report notes that it is large and how long the scan took, with how to make it faster: scan the part that matters, or leave out a long list.

anyOf.description: a number as text, or text with a {var:…} token

waitForSelector.description: Start the scan only once this selector is on the page, for content that loads late. If it does not appear within the wait timeout, the step fails rather than scanning the page without it.

waitVisible.description: With Wait for, wait until the element is visible, not only on the page.

includeRuleIds.description: The only rules this scan runs: the rest of its level's rules do not. Name a WCAG criterion (wcag-1.4.3-contrast-minimum) to check it in full, or single checks (contrast-minimum); a criterion only some of whose checks run is reported as partly checked unless one of them fails. Use a comma separated string.

excludeRuleIds.description: Rule IDs to exclude for this scan only. Use a comma separated string.

includeTags.description: Run only the rules with these tags, within the scan's WCAG version and level (rules that test no WCAG criterion, such as best practices, as tagged). Their criteria are reported as with Include rules: partly checked when some of a criterion's checks do not run. Use a comma separated string.

excludeTags.description: Rule tags to exclude for this scan only. Use a comma separated string.

includeMode.description: With both Include rules and Include tags: run only the rules that are in both, or every rule that is in either.

engineMode.description: Auditor support makes the assumptions an auditor would where the page leaves something unset, such as a white background behind the page; Strict conformance assumes nothing the page does not state.

anyOf.description: text with a {var:…} token

findingsSource.description: Whether findings are reported per WCAG success criterion, gathering the checks behind each one, or per single check, or both.

anyOf.description: text with a {var:…} token

screenshotView.description: Take a screenshot of the page once the scan is done, shown with its results. Set to false for a scan that needs no picture of the page: it runs faster and its report is smaller. Pictures of the flagged elements (Element screenshots) are set apart.

elementScreenshots.description: Take a picture of each element surea11y flags, with a box around it, shown beside its finding. A finding that shows only with the WCAG text spacing applied also gets a picture with the spacing applied, beside the one of the page as it is.

action.setColorScheme.title: Set color scheme and contrast
action.setColorScheme.description: Show the page in the light or dark color scheme, in high contrast, or both, as a browser or system set to them would. The color scheme sets prefers-color-scheme, which the page's media queries follow; until a step sets it, the page is shown as the run's configuration says (the browser's default, light, unless it says otherwise), and Run default goes back to that. High contrast shows the page in forced colors, as Windows' contrast themes do: the browser replaces the page's colors with the user's, and its forced-colors media queries and system colors such as Canvas and GrayText follow, so a scan or a screenshot shows what stays visible then (focus indicators, icons, borders of controls). Leave either one empty to keep it as it is. Both stay until another step changes them, across navigation. A site with its own theme switch that does not follow prefers-color-scheme needs a click on that switch instead. surea11y still measures contrast in the page's own colors in high contrast, as WCAG asks, and each scan says it was taken in it. High contrast needs Chrome.

action.setLanguage.title: Set language
action.setLanguage.description: Show the page in a language, as a browser set to it would: the Accept-Language header a server picks a language by, navigator.language and navigator.languages for a site that picks it in its scripts, and the format of dates and numbers. It stays set until another Set language step changes it, across navigation, refreshes and pages the workflow opens. The open page loads again so it shows the new language now; a page that has not loaded yet picks it up when it does. Run default goes back to the language the run started with: its configuration's, or the browser's own when it sets none. Each scan says the language it was taken in, and warns when the page declares another (its html lang): a site that keeps its language in a cookie, an account setting or its address (such as /en/), or picks it by location, may not follow this step. Dates and numbers need Chrome.

action.mergedScan.description: Report the A11y scans inside it as one scan: the same view scanned in several contexts (light and dark theme, desktop and mobile width) counts once. Each scan inside is a context, named by its label; a failure lists the contexts it occurs in, and one whose result differs between contexts (a different contrast ratio, a different size) is listed once per result. The merged scan holds every context's screenshot. Variables set inside stay available after it. A Merged scan cannot contain another.

scanTags.description: The merged scan's tags, used to filter the report by tag and to break the live totals down. The tags of the scans inside describe their contexts and are shown with them; when this is empty, the merged scan takes all of theirs. Supports {var:name}, {index}, {oneBased}, {total}.

actions.description: The steps to run, with an A11y scan for each context. A scan with no label is named by its place, as "Scan 2 of 4".

action.skipIteration.title: Skip iteration
action.skipIteration.description: Inside a loop (For each element, Repeat or Crawl), skip the rest of the current item when its conditions match, and go on with the next one. Each field you fill in is one condition: Selector exists; each check on the element of Element selector (Text equals, Text contains, Attribute equals, Attribute contains, or Attribute name alone for having it); URL includes; Variable equals. The item is skipped when all of them match, or, with Use OR, when any of them does. A step with no condition never skips. Text checks are case-sensitive and read the text with its spaces collapsed. In a Crawl, a skipped page's links are not followed.

runSpec.title: surea11y-lab run spec
runSpec.description: surea11y-lab run spec: A workflow run: the page to open, the steps to take there and how to scan. The app saves one inside every configuration (its "runSpec"), and `node src/cli/run-workflow.js <spec.json>` runs one; add --check to validate it without running.

url.description: The page the workflow starts on, http or https.

scenarioName.description: Names the run, and the folder the CLI keeps its runs in.

viewport.description: A preset name, or a size in CSS pixels.

colorScheme.description: The color scheme the page is shown in as the run starts (prefers-color-scheme). Left out, the browser's own (light). Set color scheme and contrast changes it; its Run default comes back to this.

highContrast.description: Show the page in forced colors (high contrast) as the run starts. Left out, off. Its Run default comes back to this.

language.description: The language the page is shown in as the run starts, as a BCP 47 tag (es-ES, de, pt-BR), or a variable such as {var:lang}, so each batch row can set its own. Left out, the browser's own. Set language changes it; its Run default comes back to this.

acceptUntrustedCerts.description: Open sites whose certificate the browser does not trust: a staging server's self-signed one, or any site through a network that inspects HTTPS. Left out, off, and such a site fails the run saying why. The browser cannot then tell a site from one pretending to be it, so a run that signs in should not use it on a network you do not trust. A run that uses it says so in its log and in runDiagnostics.untrustedCertsAccepted.
